blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 87 in June to 85 in September (−2.3%), and it took 16.2% of the city’s 240 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 143 in June to 131 in September (−8.4%), and it took 23.7% of the city’s 375 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out King George Corridor for detached houses in June (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in September (a sellers’ best bet).

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in King George Corridor than in June?
faq.a: In King George Corridor, listings of houses fell from 87 in June to 85 in September (−2.3%); condos and townhomes fell from 143 in June to 131 in September (−8.4%).

faq.q: How big is King George Corridor compared with the rest of South Surrey and White Rock?
faq.a: In September 2026, King George Corridor held 14.2% of the 600 houses listed in South Surrey and White Rock and 22.1% of the 593 condos and townhomes listed in South Surrey and White Rock.

faq.q: How many homes sold in King George Corridor from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 39 houses and 89 condos and townhomes sold in King George Corridor over those 4 months.
